description: Before electricity, the night was different. Every episode puts you inside one era’s worst nights — the plague years, the Victorian slums, the villages that feared what knocked after dark — and shows you exactly what living through it was like. No kings, no generals. Just you, a lantern, and whatever was waiting outside.

videos.title: The Deadly Fog That Swallowed Victorian London
Locked in Your House With the Plague — London, 1665
Lanterns Out — History's Darkest Nights, As If You Were There
Victorian London's Worst Job Started at Midnight (1850)
Why Appalachian Families Never Answered a Knock After Dark (1894)
How Did People Sleep During the Black Death? (Florence, 1348)
